title: Words are inverted in text extractor when I extract
summary: Text Extractor returned English words in reverse order in the reported example.

judgment.rationale: A maintainer could not reproduce the sample; the reporter answered the regional-settings question, but the selected OCR language remains unclear.
evidence: On 0.86.0 the reported result was Function Axis Horizontal instead of Horizontal Axis Function; a sample image is linked.
A maintainer obtained the expected order and asked about regional settings; the reporter said Saudi Arabia and changing region to US or UK did not help.
Current OcrTextFormatter reverses space-separated words when the OCR language culture is right-to-left; this does not establish the language selected or the cause in the historical version.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask which OCR language was selected during the sample extraction and reproduce against that language.

fix_assessment.rationale: An ordering correction may be applicable once the selected OCR language and current behavior are confirmed.

proposed_fixes.title: Investigate OCR word ordering by selected language
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: language-dependent ordering may reverse the English words; the original selected recognizer and failing path are not established.
plan: Identify the OCR language selected for the supplied example and reproduce on a current build.
Compare recognizer output and formatted text for English and right-to-left language selections.
Correct only a confirmed ordering error without breaking right-to-left or mixed-script content.
Add focused regression tests for English and right-to-left examples, including punctuation.
verification: The supplied English example appears in reading order with the matching OCR language.
Right-to-left and mixed-script text retain correct ordering.

confidence.rationale: A relevant current code path exists, but the reporter’s OCR selection and current behavior remain unknown.

issue_context.summary: Text Extractor returned English words in reverse order in the reported example.
known_information: On 0.86.0 the reported result was Function Axis Horizontal instead of Horizontal Axis Function; a sample image is linked.
A maintainer obtained the expected order and asked about regional settings; the reporter said Saudi Arabia and changing region to US or UK did not help.
inferences: A selected right-to-left OCR language could affect ordering in current code, but the reporter’s actual selected recognizer is unclear.
initial_investigation: Inspected src/modules/PowerOCR/PowerOCR.Core/Formatting/OcrTextFormatter.cs and TextExtractorService.cs: current region formatting reverses words for RTL language cultures.
Reviewed complete thread including the answered region question, no assignee and no timeline fix; searched upstream PRs without establishing a covering fix.
issue_context.analysis: Do not repeat the already answered region question. Identify the selected OCR recognizer language, which is not the same as Windows region.

information_gaps.information: The OCR language selected in Text Extractor when the example is extracted.
information_gaps.why_needed: Distinguishes recognizer-language ordering from the already-tested Windows region.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reply with the language shown in Text Extractor while extracting the existing example.

comment.body: Thanks for confirming that changing the Windows region did not help. For the existing example, which OCR language was selected in Text Extractor when you extracted the text? The OCR selection can differ from the Windows region and will help reproduce the ordering.
